title: The spotlight at the Monogram Theater
summary: Punch tells how a spotlight startled him into missing notes during a Sunday solo at the Monogram.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: I wanted to play the Fresh Can Tea in Chicago. Lewis had been playing in the place to call the Monogram Theater, Steep and 35th Street. So Lewis was playing and he just called me up and told me to go ahead and the highest of what I'm got week, and get three numbers, you know, to get on the stage with Dad. Every Sunday, you know, get on stage. That'd be packed jammed with most kids though, you know. And what got me, if they would have told me about it, well it wouldn't have did me so bad, see. And what I wanted to do is just as I jump up and take a solo and a big light like that, see. But the light was out. And it wasn't far from my head by that floor, you see. And I jump up and take a solo and they throw that light on. Man, I must have missed about six notes. That light scared the devil out of me, man. Because I didn't know, you know, they were going to throw it. I just thought I was waiting from the spotlight. They throw that thing right in the middle of my head, man. I'm joking, I thought something was falling. But everybody laughed and seemed to be a joke, so I just went on and blow it then.
Well you should have did that little routine every Sunday then, make them think it's part of the act.
